components.title: The Water Cycle
components.subtitle: Understand how water continuously moves through Earth's atmosphere, land, and oceans.

components.title: Journey of a Single Drop
components.subtitle: The Earth's water is a fixed volume, constantly recycled through evaporation, condensation, and precipitation.

components.text: Core Concepts of the Water Cycle

components.label: STAGE 1
components.title: Evaporation and Transpiration
components.Body: Solar energy heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, causing it to change from liquid to gas (vapor) via evaporation. Additionally, plants release moisture from their leaves into the atmosphere through transpiration.

components.label: STAGE 2
components.title: Condensation and Cloud Formation
components.Body: As warm water vapor rises, it cools and condenses into tiny liquid water droplets or ice crystals around microscopic particles in the air, eventually forming clouds and fog.

components.label: STAGE 3
components.title: Precipitation and Collection
components.Body: When condensed water droplets in clouds become too heavy to remain suspended by updrafts, they fall back to Earth as rain, snow, sleet, or hail. This water collects in bodies of water and infiltrates the soil.

components.label: WORKED EXAMPLE
components.title: Tracing a Raindrop from Mountain to Ocean
components.Body: Consider a snowflake landing on a high alpine peak. When temperatures rise, it melts into liquid water (run-off), flows into a mountain stream, joins a major river system, and eventually flows back into the ocean, ready to evaporate again.
components.code: Precipitation -> Runoff -> Stream -> River -> Ocean -> Evaporation
components.code_caption: The complete circular pathway of global hydrology.
components.takeaway: Water never truly leaves the planetary system; it merely changes states and locations.

questions.question: What process converts liquid water from plant leaves into atmospheric water vapor?
questions.explanation: Transpiration is the specific process where plants release water vapor through microscopic pores called stomata.

questions.question: Which phase change occurs when water vapor turns into liquid water droplets in clouds?
questions.explanation: Condensation is the cooling of water vapor back into liquid droplets, forming clouds.

questions.question: Where does the energy that drives the entire water cycle primarily originate?
questions.explanation: Solar energy from the Sun provides the heat required to evaporate water from oceans and land surfaces.
